paper.title: Cost-Effective Online Multi-LLM Selection with Versatile Reward Models

settings.name_in_paper: C2MAB-V: cost-effective combinatorial multi-armed bandit with versatile reward models (AWC / SUC / AIC) under long-term budget constraint
unmapped: Reward functions: Any Win (1-prod(1-mu_k)), Sum Up (sum mu_k), All In (prod mu_k); L-Lipschitz and monotone
Partial feedback: only a subset F_t of the selected arms is observed; o* is the minimum probability that all selected arms are observed
Each arm has an unknown stochastic cost; long-term average cost must stay below threshold rho; violation V(T) measured
Feasible sets: |S|<=N (AWC) or |S|=N (SUC/AIC); N plays the role of m
Regret is alpha-approximate with an alpha-approximation oracle (alpha=1-1/e for AWC, 1 for SUC/AIC)
settings.definition_quote: During each round $t \in \mathcal{T}$, the cloud coordinates and selects a subset $S_t$ of available LLMs from $\mathcal{K}$... Formally, the local server observes feedback from the LLM subset $\mathcal{F}_t$ in action $S_t$... there is a predetermined budget guarantee threshold $\rho > 0$ ... $V(T)=\left[ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{k \in \mathcal{F}_t} y_{t,k} -\rho \right]^{+}$ ... $R(T) = \E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T \left(\alpha \cdot r(S^*_t;\boldsymbol{\mu}) - r(S_t;\boldsymbol{\mu})\right)\right]$

bound.expression_latex: \frac{2 L}{o^*} \sqrt{2 N K T \ln \left(\frac{2 \pi^2 K T}{3 }\right)}+\left(K+1\right)r^*

symbols.o_star: minimum probability over rounds and actions that all selected arms are observed
symbols.r_star: maximum expected reward max_S r(S;mu) (<= N L)
symbols.m: N, maximum number of LLMs selected per action

conditions: reward function r(S;mu) is monotone and L-Lipschitz
alpha-approximation oracle (alpha=1-1/e for AWC, 1 for SUC/AIC)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: With $\delta=1/T$ in the confidence radius, the $\alpha$-approximate regret for the multi-LLM selection problem is bounded as follows, with probability at least $1-1/T$: R(T) \leq \frac{2 L}{o^*} \sqrt{2 N K T \ln \left(\frac{2 \pi^2 K T}{3 }\right)}+\left(K+1\right)r^*.

results.notes: R(T) is defined as an expectation but the theorem states it holds w.p. at least 1-1/T; recorded as high probability as stated. Feedback mapped to triggered_semi_bandit (partial observation of selected arms with probability o*).

symbols.m: N, maximum number of LLMs selected per action

conditions: worst case S_t = F_t (all selected LLMs used)

source.label: thm:violation
source.quote: With $\delta=1/T$ in the confidence radius, the constraint violation under the worst case is bounded as follows, with probability at least $1-1/T$: V(T) \leq \sqrt{NK/T} \left(2 \sqrt{2\ln \left(\frac{2 \pi^2 K T}{3 }\right)}+\sqrt{NK/T}\right).

results.notes: Bound on average per-round budget violation V(T) = [ (1/T) sum costs - rho ]^+, not a regret; recorded as stated (not multiplied by T). Proof sketch's terms don't obviously match the final expression.

cited_results.cited_title: Tight regret bounds for stochastic combinatorial semi-bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic combinatorial semi-bandit with linear reward, full semi-bandit feedback, at most N base arms per action
